text:
This looks like the period just after the 2013 taper tantrum. Unemployment at 7.4% points to mid-2013 (June or July). The 10-year yield at 2.75% is up 0.59 over 3 months, and the 12-month change is +1.18. The 10-year was about 1.6% in mid-2012 and about 2.5% in June 2013, so the month may be a little later, but the data are mixed.

Equity returns of -4.1% over 1 month fit June 2013, when the S&P fell about 1.5%. A 12-month equity gain of +18% fits June 2013 (S&P was up about 20%). A 1-month gold gain of +6.3% fits a July 2013 bounce, since gold fell in June and rose about 1% in July. But -4.1% for equities in one month fits August 2013, when the S&P fell about 3% and the 10-year was about 2.75%. Gold rose about 6% in August 2013, which is consistent. Unemployment in August 2013 was 7.3%, and was 7.4% as first reported at the time. Headline CPI at 1.96% YoY is consistent with August 2013 (1.5% in the year to July, 1.2% in June, and 1.5% in August). The 3-month change in headline CPI of +0.85 fits a rise from 1.1% in May to 1.96%. The 12-month change of +0.52 fits August 2012 CPI at 1.7%. Everything points to August 2013, though the CPI value is a bit high. Emerging-market equities at -4.3% for 1 month also fit August 2013.

Alternatively, this could be September 2013, but the equity return for that month was positive. August 2013 is the best fit.
